Et videte a locis sublimibus insanias multas, id est vitia idololatriæ, aliaque irrationabilissima scelera, quæ naturalis ratio detestatur, in medio ejus, puta Samariæ; videte quoque et calumniam patientes, id est pauperes et simplices quibus injuriantur potentes ac divites, in penetralibus ejus, id est secretioribus habitaculis Samariæ.
paras.en: Next God, wishing to show to all the equity of His judgments against Israel, says: [[3:9|Publish it|Auditum facite]], that is, make it known, O Prophets, or others taught by the Prophets, [[3:9|in the houses of Azotus|in ædibus Azoti]], that is, in the houses of the city of the Philistines so called, [[3:9|and in the houses of the land of Egypt|et in ædibus terræ Ægypti]]; [[3:9|and say|et dicite]]: [[3:9|Assemble yourselves|Congregamini]], that is, come together, O men of Azotus and of Egypt, [[3:9|upon the mountains of Samaria|super montes Samariæ]]. By Samaria can be understood the capital itself of the ten tribes, or the whole province, which is full of mountains. [[3:9|and behold|Et videte]] from the high places [[3:9|the many follies|insanias multas]], that is, the vices of idolatry and other most irrational crimes, which natural reason abhors, [[3:9|in the midst thereof|in medio ejus]], namely of Samaria; behold also [[3:9|them that suffer oppression|et calumniam patientes]], that is, the poor and simple, whom the powerful and rich wrong, [[3:9|in the inner rooms thereof|in penetralibus ejus]], that is, in the more hidden dwellings of Samaria.

paras.t: Et nescierunt decem tribus facere rectum, dicit Dominus, id est opera bona et justa, quoniam excæcavit eos sua malitia. Sed ista ignorantia juris, seu desiderata, non excusat. De talibus loquitur Jeremias: Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt. Thesaurizantes iniquitatem, id est peccata peccatis adjicientes, et incessabiliter accumulantes, et rapinam, id est bona aliis violenter ablata, in ædibus, id est domibus suis, in quibus ista spoliata reponunt.
paras.en: [[3:10|And they have not known|Et nescierunt]], the ten tribes, [[3:10|to do the right thing, saith the Lord|facere rectum, dicit Dominus]], that is, good and just works, since their malice blinded them. But this ignorance of the law, being as it were desired [that is, wilful ignorance, which does not excuse but rather aggravates the sin], does not excuse. Of such men Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 4:22|they are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge|Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt]]. [[3:10|storing up iniquity|Thesaurizantes iniquitatem]], that is, adding sins to sins and heaping them up without ceasing, [[3:10|and robberies|et rapinam]], that is, goods taken from others by violence, [[3:10|in their houses|in ædibus]], that is, in their dwellings, in which they store up these spoils.

paras.t: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Tribulabitur et circuietur terra, id est, plebs decem tribuum ab Assyriis affligetur et circumdata erit. Quod factum est tempore Salmanasar regis Assyriorum. Et detrahetur ex te fortitudo tua, id est regia dignitas seu potestas; vel, potentes tui, o decem tribus, superabuntur; et diripientur ædes tuæ, id est, habitacula tua spoliabuntur ac destruentur.
paras.en: [[3:11|Therefore thus saith the Lord God|Propterea hæc dicit Dominus Deus]]: [[3:11|The land shall be in tribulation, and shall be compassed about|Tribulabitur et circuietur terra]], that is, the people of the ten tribes will be afflicted and surrounded by the Assyrians. This was done in the time of Salmanasar king of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:3||]][[4 Kings 17:6||]]. [[3:11|and thy strength shall be taken away from thee|Et detrahetur ex te fortitudo tua]], that is, the royal dignity or power; or, thy mighty men, O ten tribes, will be overcome; [[3:11|and thy houses shall be spoiled|et diripientur ædes tuæ]], that is, thy dwellings will be plundered and destroyed.

paras.t: Quoniam tamen non omnes de decem tribubus perituri erant, subjungitur (utitur quoque Amos parabola sumpta ex suo officio): Hæc dicit Dominus: Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura aut extremum auriculæ, id est parvas paucasque reliquias; sic eruentur filii Israel qui habitant in Samaria, id est provincia illa, ita quod pauci eorum evadent sævitiam Assyriorum, in plaga lectuli et in Damasci grabato: id est, isti qui corporaliter habitabant in Samaria, habitabant, id est animo quiescebant, in plaga, id est regione, lectuli, id est regis ac populi Syriæ: quia Phacee rex Israel et populus ejus vel etiam posteri, in Rasin rege Syriæ et populo ejus confidebant, quos conduxerunt ad pugnandum contra Juda tempore Achaz; sicque in eis et in grabato Damasci, id est populo urbis illius, quasi in lecto quiescebant, magnam in illis habendo fiduciam. Sic exponit Hieronymus. Alii autem exponunt sic: In plaga lectuli, id est, prædicti ab Assyriis eruentur, et morabuntur seu erunt, postquam evaserunt, in regione Juda, quæ dicitur lectulus propter templum situm in ea, quod erat quasi lectus Sponsi cœlestis. Unde secundo Paralipomenon scriptum est, quod quidam eorum ad exhortationem Ezechiæ venerunt Jerusalem et ad cultum Dei conversi sunt. Aliqui vero ad Damascum fugerunt, ut dicunt: ideoque subjungitur, In Damasci grabato.
paras.en: Since, however, not all of the ten tribes were to perish, there is added (and Amos uses a parable taken from his own calling): [[3:12|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[3:12|As if a shepherd should get out of the lion's mouth two legs, or the tip of the ear|Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura aut extremum auriculæ]], that is, small and scanty remnants; [[3:12|so shall the children of Israel be taken out that dwell in Samaria|sic eruentur filii Israel qui habitant in Samaria]], that is, in that province, so that few of them will escape the savagery of the Assyrians, [[3:12|in a place of a bed, and in the couch of Damascus|in plaga lectuli et in Damasci grabato]]: that is, those who dwelt bodily in Samaria dwelt, that is, rested in mind, *in the place*, that is, the region, *of a bed*, that is, of the king and people of Syria: for Phacee king of Israel and his people, or also their descendants, trusted in Rasin king of Syria and his people, whom they hired to fight against Juda in the time of Achaz[[4 Kings 16:5||]]; and so they rested in them, and *in the couch of Damascus*, that is, in the people of that city, as in a bed, putting great trust in them. So Jerome expounds it. But others expound it thus: *In a place of a bed*, that is, the aforesaid will be taken out from the Assyrians, and will stay or be, after they have escaped, in the region of Juda, which is called a bed because of the temple situated in it, which was as it were the bed of the heavenly Bridegroom. Hence it is written in the second book of Paralipomenon that some of them, at the exhortation of Ezechias, came to Jerusalem and were converted to the worship of God[[2 Par 30:11||]]. Others, as they say, fled to Damascus; and therefore it is added, *In the couch of Damascus*.

paras.t: Audite, o Prophetæ, revelationes prophetales auribus cordis, et contestamini, id est, cum attestatione seu firmiter prædicate eas, in domo Jacob, id est familia decem tribuum descendentium de semine Jacob, dicit Dominus Deus exercituum.
paras.en: [[3:13|Hear ye|Audite]], O Prophets, the prophetic revelations with the ears of the heart, [[3:13|and testify|et contestamini]], that is, preach them with solemn witness, or firmly, [[3:13|in the house of Jacob|in domo Jacob]], that is, in the family of the ten tribes descended from the seed of Jacob, [[3:13|saith the Lord the God of hosts|dicit Dominus Deus exercituum]].

paras.t: Quia in die quum visitare cœpero prævaricationes Israel super eum, id est, quum per regem Assyriorum Salmanasar cœpero peccata decem tribuum vindicare in eas, visitabo super altaria Bethel, id est, sacrilega altaria facta in urbe nomine Bethel, destruam per Assyrios; et amputabuntur cornua altaris principalis aurei vituli, qui positus fuit in Bethel, et cadent in terram: Assyrii namque omnia loca et fana idololatriæ decem tribuum destruxerunt.
paras.en: [[3:14|That in the day when I shall begin to visit the transgressions of Israel|Quia in die quum visitare cœpero prævaricationes Israel]] [[3:14|upon him|super eum]], that is, when through Salmanasar king of the Assyrians I shall begin to punish the sins of the ten tribes upon them, [[3:14|I will visit|visitabo]] [[3:14|upon the altars of Bethel|super altaria Bethel]], that is, I will destroy through the Assyrians the sacrilegious altars made in the city named Bethel[[3 Kings 12:32||]] [the margin reads III Reg. xxii, 32; the altar at Bethel is at 3 Kings 12:32]; [[3:14|and the horns of the altars shall be cut off|et amputabuntur cornua altaris]], the chief altar, of the golden calf that was set up in Bethel, [[3:14|and shall fall to the ground|et cadent in terram]]: for the Assyrians destroyed all the places and shrines of idolatry of the ten tribes.

paras.t: Et percutiam domum hiemalem cum domo æstiva, id est, omnes domos earum, tam illas in quibus manebant tempore hiemali seu frigido, quam illas in quibus æstivo tempore morabantur, per exercitum Assyriorum demoliar. Quamvis enim Assyrii ista fecerunt mala intentione et cum gravi peccato, Deus tamen juste induxit eos ad hæc, tanquam ad rem bonam seu justam punitionem. Potentes autem et divites decem tribuum, duas domos habebant: unam hiemalem, respicientem ad austrum, unde calidus ventus exsurgit; aliam æstivalem, versam ad aquilonem, unde frigidus nascitur ventus: ut secundum varietatem temporum, apta ac delectabilia habitacula inhabitarent. Et peribunt domus eburneæ: qualem legitur Achab ædificasse. Dicuntur autem eburneæ, quoniam quædam structuræ de ebore factæ, erant in eis. Et dissipabuntur ædes multæ, dicit Dominus. Assyrii enim plurimas domos subverterunt.
paras.en: [[3:15|And I will strike the winter house with the summer house|Et percutiam domum hiemalem cum domo æstiva]], that is, I will pull down by the army of the Assyrians all their houses, both those in which they lived in the winter or cold season and those in which they stayed in the summer season. For although the Assyrians did these things with an evil intention and with grievous sin, God nevertheless justly led them to it, as to a good thing, that is, a just punishment. Now the powerful and rich of the ten tribes had two houses: one for winter, facing the south, whence the warm wind rises; the other for summer, turned towards the north, whence the cold wind springs: so that, according to the change of seasons, they might live in fitting and pleasant dwellings. [[3:15|and the houses of ivory shall perish|Et peribunt domus eburneæ]]: such a one as Achab is read to have built[[3 Kings 22:39||]]. And they are called houses of ivory because certain parts of their structure were made of ivory. [[3:15|and many houses shall be destroyed, saith the Lord|Et dissipabuntur ædes multæ, dicit Dominus]]. For the Assyrians overthrew very many houses.

3.title: Explanatio moralis ejusdem capituli tertii.
3.title_en: Moral explanation of the same third chapter.

paras.t: Quod in principio hujus capituli ad populum Israel dicitur, ad Ecclesiam Christi refertur, ut sit sensus: Audite auribus cordis et corporis, verbum quod locutus est Dominus super vos, filii Israel, id est, filii Ecclesiæ, seu plebs christiana, quæ Deum fide videndo es Israel (qui interpretatur, videns Deum), super omnem cognationem quam eduxi de terra Ægypti, id est super omnem Ecclesiam, quam eduxi de conversatione mundana et præsenti sæculo nequam, transferens eam in regnum Filii dilectionis meæ, id est in mysticam unitatem credentium per fidem et caritatem. Tantummodo vos cognovi ex omnibus cognationibus terræ: id est, postquam prædicata est fides christiana et publicata, solos Christianos cognovi et nosco per approbationem. De qua cognitione dicit Apostolus: Si quis diligit Deum, hic cognitus est ab eo; et rursus, Si quis ignorat, ignorabit. Interim enim nullus extra Ecclesiam est salvatus, nec potest salvari, sicut nec extra arcam Noe quisquam ab aquis diluvii exstitit præservatus. Propter quod ait Salvator: Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit; qui vero non crediderit, condemnabitur. Idcirco visitabo super vos omnes iniquitates vestras, id est, in præsenti vos castigabo, ne æternaliter pereatis. De hoc in præcedentibus dicta sunt multa. Beatus enim homo qui corripitur a Domino. Et Apostolus dicit: Si extra disciplinam estis, ergo adulteri et non filii estis.
paras.en: What is said at the beginning of this chapter to the people of Israel is referred to the Church of Christ, so that the sense is: [[3:1|Hear|Audite]] with the ears of the heart and of the body [[3:1|the word that the Lord hath spoken concerning you, O ye children of Israel|verbum quod locutus est Dominus super vos, filii Israel]], that is, children of the Church, or Christian people, who, seeing God by faith, art Israel (which is interpreted, seeing God), [[3:1|concerning the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt|super omnem cognationem quam eduxi de terra Ægypti]]: that is, concerning the whole Church, which I brought out of a worldly way of life and out of this present wicked world, translating it [[Col 1:13|into the kingdom of the Son|in regnum Filii dilectionis]] of my love, that is, into the mystical unity of those who believe, through faith and charity. [[3:2|You only have I known of all the families of the earth|Tantummodo vos cognovi ex omnibus cognationibus terræ]]: that is, since the Christian faith was preached and made known, I have known and do know the Christians alone, by approbation [that is, the knowing by which God approves and owns as his]. Of this knowing the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 8:3|if any man love God, the same is known by him|Si quis diligit Deum, hic cognitus est ab eo]]; and again: [[1 Cor 14:38|if any man know not, he shall not be known|Si quis ignorat, ignorabit]] [Denis reads *ignorabit*, "he shall not know", where the Vulgate has *ignorabitur*, "he shall not be known"]. For in the meantime no one has been saved outside the Church, nor can be saved, just as no one outside the ark of Noe was preserved from the waters of the flood[[Gen 7:23||]]. For which reason the Saviour says: [[Mark 16:16|He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved: but he that believeth not shall he condemned|Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit; qui vero non crediderit, condemnabitur]]. [[3:2|therefore will I visit upon you all your iniquities|Idcirco visitabo super vos omnes iniquitates vestras]], that is, I will chastise you in the present life, lest you perish eternally. Much has been said of this in what went before. For [[Job 5:17|Blessed is the man whom God correcteth|Beatus enim homo qui corripitur a Domino]]. And the Apostle says: [[Heb 12:8|if you be without chastisement|Si extra disciplinam estis]], [[Heb 12:8|then are you bastards and not sons|ergo adulteri et non filii estis]].

paras.t: Numquid ambulabunt duo pariter, nisi convenerit eis? Sic duo non possunt simul conversari in schola Christi, vel ambulare in via virtutum, et de bono in melius efficaciter proficiendo, nisi motus passionum, iram, contentionem, impatientiamque abjiciant, et pari proposito honestaque amicitia copulentur. Quod si ita fuerint convenientes, seu concorditer consentientes in desiderio proficiendi, poterunt omni die fortissime progredi in semitis Dei, se invicem exhortando, increpando, ædificando, et pro se invicem indesinenter atque ferventer orando. Unde in Ecclesiastico legitur: Cum viro sancto assiduus esto, et quemcumque cognoveris observantem timorem Dei, cujus anima est secundum animam tuam; et alibi, Omnis homo sibi similis sociabitur. Hæc est salubris societas: siquidem væ soli; et frater adjuvans fratrem, quasi urbs munita, juxta Salomonem.
paras.en: [[3:3|Shall two walk together except they be agreed?|Numquid ambulabunt duo pariter, nisi convenerit eis?]] So two cannot live together in the school of Christ, or walk in the way of the virtues, going on effectually from good to better, unless they cast off the motions of the passions, anger, contention and impatience, and are joined by a like purpose and an honest friendship. But if they are thus agreed, or of one mind in the desire of going forward, they will be able every day to advance most strongly in the paths of God, exhorting, rebuking and edifying one another, and praying for one another unceasingly and fervently. Hence we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 37:15|be continually with a holy man, whomsoever thou shalt know to observe the fear of God|Cum viro sancto assiduus esto, et quemcumque cognoveris observantem timorem Dei]], [[Ecclus 37:16|Whose soul is according to thy own soul|cujus anima est secundum animam tuam]]; and elsewhere: [[Ecclus 13:20|every man shall associate himself to his like|Omnis homo sibi similis sociabitur]]. This is a wholesome fellowship: for [[Eccles 4:10|woe to him that is alone|væ soli]]; and [[Prov 18:19|A brother that is helped by his brother, is like a strong city|frater adjuvans fratrem, quasi urbs munita]] [Denis has *frater adjuvans fratrem*, "a brother helping his brother"], according to Solomon.

paras.t: Auditum facite in ædibus Azoti et in ædibus terræ Ægypti, id est, infidelibus annuntiate; et dicite: Congregamini super montes Samariæ, id est Ecclesiæ, quæ se dicit custodire præcepta justitiæ. Samaria enim interpretatur custoditio. Et videte insanias multas in medio ejus, id est, peccata Christianorum perpendite, ut quum videritis eos ab adversariis fidei superari, vel divinitus castigari, non blasphemetis nomen Christi, quasi non possit Ecclesiam suam tueri, nec vestræ potestati aut diis vestris attribuatis victoriam qua prævaletis fidelibus; sed justum Dei judicium considerate, qui propter peccata Christianorum, tradit eosdem adversariis suis, ac aliis plagis corripit eos.
paras.en: [[3:9|Publish it in the houses of Azotus, and in the houses of the land of Egypt|Auditum facite in ædibus Azoti et in ædibus terræ Ægypti]], that is, proclaim it to the unbelievers; [[3:9|and say: Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria|et dicite: Congregamini super montes Samariæ]], that is, of the Church, which says that she keeps the precepts of justice. For *Samaria* is interpreted "keeping". [[3:9|and behold the many follies in the midst thereof|Et videte insanias multas in medio ejus]]: that is, weigh the sins of the Christians, so that, when you see them overcome by the adversaries of the faith, or chastised by God, you may not blaspheme the name of Christ, as though he could not defend his Church, nor ascribe to your own power or to your gods the victory by which you prevail over the faithful; but consider the just judgment of God, who for the sins of the Christians delivers them to his adversaries, and chastens them with other scourges.

paras.t: Qui nescierunt facere rectum. Quibus et a Jeremia dicitur: Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, et pardus varietates suas: et vos poteritis benefacere, quum didiceritis malum. Isti enim non habent scientiam illam quæ est unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti, de qua ait Scriptura: Dedit illi scientiam Sanctorum. Thesaurizantes iniquitatem et rapinam in ædibus suis. Quibus dicitur a Jacobo: Thesaurizastis vobis iram in die judicii. Et ad Romanos Apostolus: Ignoras quoniam benignitas Dei ad pœnitentiam te adducit? An divitias bonitatis et patientiæ et longanimitatis Dei contemnis? Secundum duritiam autem tuam et impœnitens cor tuum, thesaurizas tibi iram in die iræ et revelationis justi judicii Dei. Tales sunt habituati et indurati in vitiis: qui non ex passione, sed animi deliberatione et habitu peccant.
paras.en: Who [[3:10|have not known to do the right thing|nescierunt facere rectum]]. To whom it is also said by Jeremias: [[Jer 13:23|If the Ethiopian can change his skin, or the leopard his spots: you also may do well, when you have learned evil|Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, et pardus varietates suas: et vos poteritis benefacere, quum didiceritis malum]]. For these have not that knowledge which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]], of which the Scripture says: [[Wis 10:10|gave him the knowledge of the holy things|Dedit illi scientiam Sanctorum]] [*scientiam sanctorum*, which can also be read "the knowledge of the saints"]. [[3:10|storing up iniquity, and robberies in their houses|Thesaurizantes iniquitatem et rapinam in ædibus suis]]. To whom it is said by James: [[Jas 5:3|You have stored up to yourselves wrath|Thesaurizastis vobis iram]] in the day of judgment [Denis has *in die judicii*, "in the day of judgment", where the Vulgate has *in novissimis diebus*, "against the last days"]. And the Apostle to the Romans: [[Rom 2:4|Knowest thou not that the benignity of God leadeth thee to penance?|Ignoras quoniam benignitas Dei ad pœnitentiam te adducit?]] [[Rom 2:4|Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and patience and longsuffering?|An divitias bonitatis et patientiæ et longanimitatis Dei contemnis?]] [[Rom 2:5|But according to thy hardness and impenitent heart, thou treasurest up to thyself wrath, against the day of wrath and revelation of the just judgment of God|Secundum duritiam autem tuam et impœnitens cor tuum, thesaurizas tibi iram in die iræ et revelationis justi judicii Dei]]. Such men are habituated and hardened in vices: they sin not from passion, but from deliberation of mind and from habit.

paras.t: Horum terra, id est corpora, tribulabuntur in igne æterno, et a dæmonibus circumdabuntur. Fortitudo quoque eorum penitus detrahetur. Quoniam gloria impii, stercus et vermis: hodie extollitur, et cras non invenitur.
paras.en: Their [[3:11|land|terra]], that is, their bodies, shall be in tribulation in the everlasting fire, and shall be compassed about by the devils. Their [[3:11|strength|Fortitudo]] too shall be wholly taken away. For the glory of the wicked [[1 Mach 2:62|is dung and worms|gloria impii, stercus et vermis]]: [[1 Mach 2:63|Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow he shall not be found|hodie extollitur, et cras non invenitur]].

paras.t: Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura, etc., id est, quamvis leo ille sævissimus, qui est diabolus, multos fidelium devoret, absorbens fluvium nec admirans; aliqui tamen, puta electi, qui pauci sunt, dentes ejus evadunt per gratiam Christi summi pastoris, et per instructionem ac bonam præsidentiam prælatorum. Potest hoc quoque referri ad Judæos conversos ad Christum, qui aliis plurimis pereuntibus, atque a dæmonibus per infidelitatem devoratis, erepti sunt. De quibus dicit Apostolus: Reliquiæ per electionem gratiæ salvæ factæ sunt; et Isaias, Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma essemus.
paras.en: [[3:12|As if a shepherd should get out of the lion's mouth two legs|Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura]], etc.: that is, although that most cruel lion, who is the devil, devours many of the faithful[[1 Pet 5:8||]], drinking up a river and not wondering[[Job 40:18||]], yet some, namely the elect, who are few[[Matt 20:16||]], escape his teeth through the grace of Christ the chief shepherd[[John 10:11||]][[John 10:14||]], and through the instruction and good government of prelates. This may also be referred to the Jews converted to Christ, who were snatched away while very many others perished and were devoured by the devils through unbelief. Of whom the Apostle says: [[Rom 11:5|a remnant saved according to the election of grace|Reliquiæ per electionem gratiæ salvæ factæ sunt]]; and Isaias: [[Is 1:9|Except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom|Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma essemus]].

paras.t: Contestamini, id est prædicate, o doctores et pastores Ecclesiæ, in domo Jacob, id est in populo vitiis reluctante, qui sunt spiritualiter filii Jacob, qui interpretatur supplantans. Quia quum visitare cœpero prævaricationes Israel, id est peccata Ecclesiæ castigare. Tempus enim est ut judicium incipiat a domo Dei. Et per Ezechielem loquitur Dominus: A sanctuario meo incipite percutere. Visitabo super altaria Bethel, id est schismaticorum ac hæreticorum, qui se præ ceteris jactant esse in domo Dei, vel domum ipsius. Bethel autem interpretatur domus Dei.
paras.en: [[3:13|testify|Contestamini]], that is, preach, O doctors and pastors of the Church, [[3:13|in the house of Jacob|in domo Jacob]], that is, among the people that wrestles against vices, who are spiritually the children of Jacob, which is interpreted "supplanter"[[Gen 25:25||]]. For [[3:14|when I shall begin to visit the transgressions of Israel|quum visitare cœpero prævaricationes Israel]], that is, to chastise the sins of the Church. For [[1 Pet 4:17|the time is, that judgment should begin at the house of God|Tempus enim est ut judicium incipiat a domo Dei]]. And the Lord speaks by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 9:6|begin ye at my sanctuary|A sanctuario meo incipite]] to strike. [[3:14|I will visit upon|Visitabo super]] [[3:14|the altars of Bethel|altaria Bethel]], that is, of the schismatics and heretics, who boast above others that they are in the house of God, or are his house. Now *Bethel* is interpreted "house of God".

paras.t: Et percutiam domum hiemalem, id est congregationem eorum in quibus refriguit calor sanctæ dilectionis et ignis Spiritus Sancti: in quibus est frigus constringens, id est peccatum mentem indurans, et lapideam faciens, ne capax sit gratiæ Dei et compunctionis internæ; cum domo æstiva, id est cum illis in quibus est ignis concupiscentiæ, calor iræ ac vitiorum. Et peribunt domus eburneæ, id est collectio eorum qui a foris virtuosi videntur ac splendidi, intus autem sunt pleni sordibus culpæ; et item omnes vani, curiosi, et sæculariter adornati, quærentes placere mundo magis quam Deo. Quales fuerunt, de quibus scriptum est in Luca: Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus; Deus autem novit corda vestra: quia quod altum est hominibus, abominatio est ante Deum. Et Psalmista: Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent. Et dissipabuntur ædes multæ: id est, multi eorum qui ad tempus sunt templum Spiritus Sancti, quando in caritate consistunt, a dæmonibus superantur, destruuntur, et omne spirituale esse gratiæ gratum facientis amittunt, ita quod nil reputantur a Deo.
paras.en: [[3:15|And I will strike the winter house|Et percutiam domum hiemalem]], that is, the congregation of those in whom the warmth of holy love and the fire of the Holy Ghost have grown cold[[Matt 24:12||]]: in whom there is a binding cold, that is, sin hardening the mind and making it stony, so that it cannot receive the grace of God and inward compunction; [[3:15|with the summer house|cum domo æstiva]], that is, with those in whom is the fire of concupiscence, the heat of anger and of the vices. [[3:15|and the houses of ivory shall perish|Et peribunt domus eburneæ]], that is, the company of those who outwardly seem virtuous and splendid, but within are full of the filth of sin[[Matt 23:27||]]; and likewise all the vain, the curious, and those adorned after the fashion of the world, seeking to please the world more than God. Such were they of whom it is written in Luke: [[Luke 16:15|you are they who justify yourselves before men, but God knoweth your hearts. For that which is high to men is an abomination before God|Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus; Deus autem novit corda vestra: quia quod altum est hominibus, abominatio est ante Deum]]. And the Psalmist: [[Ps 52:6|God hath scattered the bones of them that please men|Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent]]. [[3:15|and many houses shall be destroyed|Et dissipabuntur ædes multæ]]: that is, many of those who for a time are the temple of the Holy Ghost, while they abide in charity, are overcome and destroyed by the devils, and lose all the spiritual being of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God], so that they are reckoned as nothing by God.

4.title: Expositio litteralis capituli quarti: Audite verbum hoc, vaccæ pingues.
4.title_en: Literal exposition of the fourth chapter: Hear this word, ye fat kine.

paras.t: Præterea plenius describitur in præsenti capitulo decem tribuum dira captivitas, atque horrenda punitio.
paras.en: Further, in the present chapter the dire captivity and dreadful punishment of the ten tribes is described more fully.

paras.t: Audite verbum hoc quod subditur, id est prænuntiationem calamitatis vestræ, ut territi pœniteatis, vaccæ pingues, id est, majores et potentiores ac ditiores in decem tribubus, qui recte vocamini vaccæ pingues : primo, quia jam immolandi estis Assyriis, ut mactemini; secundo, quoniam vitulos aureos adoratis, sicque impletur in vobis quod dicitur a David, Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea, et omnes qui confidunt in eis; tertio, quia per modum vaccarum, carnalem quietem et delectationes gulæ diligitis. De talibus vaccis cecinit Moyses in Deuteronomii cantico : Incrassatus est dilectus et recalcitravit; incrassatus, impinguatus, dilatatus, dereliquit Deum factorem suum. Quæ estis in monte Samariæ, id est, in regione Samariæ montuosa habitatis. Vel hoc dicitur, quoniam in montibus certis, insidiabantur his qui pergebant Jerusalem ad adorandum immolandumque Domino. Quæ calumniam facitis egenis, verbis et factis injuriando, et confringitis pauperes, eos lædendo, spoliando, occidendo, aut aliis modis persequendo; vel etiam spiritualiter illos conteritis, avertendo eos a cultu Dei. Talia quoque peccata erant in regno Juda, juxta illud Isaiæ : Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis? Quæ dicitis dominis vestris, id est regibus vel primis principibus regis vestri : Afferte, id est, date nobis licentiam afferendi seu spoliandi inferiores. Vel, Afferte, id est, date nobis de prædis, a subditis injuste sublatis : quia et reges ac judices Israel a subjectis multa extorquebant. Et bibemus, id est, spolia illa hilariter consumemus, et vina de pretio illorum potabimus. Solent enim hujusmodi oppressores pauperum, prædas cum ingenti delectatione consumere : quia et aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior.
paras.en: [[4:1|Hear this word|Audite verbum hoc]] that follows, that is, the foretelling of your calamity, so that in terror you may repent, [[4:1|ye fat kine|vaccæ pingues]]: that is, the greater, more powerful and richer men among the ten tribes, who are rightly called fat kine: first, because you are now to be offered up to the Assyrians to be slaughtered; second, because you adore golden calves, and so there is fulfilled in you what David says: [[Ps 113:16|Let them that make them become like unto them: and all such as trust in them|Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea, et omnes qui confidunt in eis]] [the margin gives Ps. cxiii, 8 "according to the Hebrew", that is, the second part of the psalm, which is v. 16 in the Vulgate numbering]; third, because after the manner of kine you love fleshly ease and the delights of the palate. Of such kine Moses sang in the canticle of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:15|The beloved grew fat, and kicked: he grew fat, and thick and gross, he forsook God who made him|Incrassatus est dilectus et recalcitravit; incrassatus, impinguatus, dilatatus, dereliquit Deum factorem suum]]. [[4:1|that are in the mountains of Samaria|Quæ estis in monte Samariæ]], that is, you dwell in the mountainous region of Samaria. Or this is said because on certain mountains they lay in wait for those who were going to Jerusalem to worship and to sacrifice to the Lord[[Osee 5:1||]] [the margin gives Osee v, 1, where the priests are a snare and a net spread upon Thabor]. [[4:1|you that oppress the needy|Quæ calumniam facitis egenis]], wronging them by word and deed, [[4:1|and crush the poor|et confringitis pauperes]], hurting, despoiling and killing them, or persecuting them in other ways; or else you crush them spiritually, turning them away from the worship of God. Such sins there were in the kingdom of Juda too, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 3:15|Why do you consume my people, and grind the faces of the poor?|Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis?]] [[4:1|that say to your masters|Quæ dicitis dominis vestris]], that is, to your kings or to the chief princes of your king: [[4:1|Bring|Afferte]], that is, give us leave to carry off, that is, to plunder, those beneath us. Or, Bring, that is, give us some of the spoils unjustly taken from subjects: for the kings and judges of Israel too extorted much from those under them. [[4:1|and we will drink|Et bibemus]], that is, we will merrily consume those spoils and drink wine bought with their price. For oppressors of the poor of this kind are wont to consume their plunder with great delight: for [[Prov 9:17|Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread is more pleasant.|aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior]]

paras.t: Quidam per vaccas pingues intelligunt uxores potentium, quæ calumniabantur egenos, quia viros suos induxerunt ad hoc. Dicebantque viris suis, id est maritis : Afferte, et bibemus.
paras.en: Some understand by the fat kine the wives of the powerful, who oppressed the needy because they led their men on to it. And they said to their men, that is, to their husbands: [[4:1|Bring, and we will drink|Afferte, et bibemus]].

paras.t: Juravit Dominus Deus in sancto suo, id est in se ipso et per se ipsum : non enim habet, per quem juret, majorem. Vel, In sancto suo, id est per me prophetam suum; vel in aliquo alio sancto homine et angelo, sicut habetur in Psalmo : Deus locutus est in sancto suo. Frequenter legitur Deus jurasse, quum tamen omnis simplex sermo ejus pro juramento habendus sit. Sed propter hominum tarditatem, certificationem, seu excitationem, jurare dignatur, quatenus insinuetur immobiliter verum esse quod ait. Quia ecce dies venient super vos, id est, tempus captivitatis et afflictionis vestræ ab Assyriis nunc instat; et levabunt vos in contis, id est, Assyrii in captivitatem vos deferent, sicut carnes pinguium vaccarum portantur in vectibus, vel negotia ponderosa in tenellis, et reliquias vestras, id est residuos, ad urbes, castra, seu latibula fugientes, levabunt in ollis ferventibus, id est in prædictis locis, in quibus quasi in ollis absconditi fuerint, concremabunt, loca talia incendendo : quæ incensa, similia erunt ollis ignitis seu bullientibus.
paras.en: [[4:2|The Lord God hath sworn by his holiness|Juravit Dominus Deus in sancto suo]] [the Latin *in sancto suo* can mean "by his holiness", "in his holy one" or "in his holy place"; Denis's readings turn on this], that is, in himself and by himself: for he has no one greater by whom to swear[[Heb 6:13||]]. Or, [[4:2|by his holiness|In sancto suo]], that is, by me, his prophet; or in some other holy man or angel, as is found in the Psalm: [[Ps 59:8|God hath spoken in his holy place|Deus locutus est in sancto suo]]. We often read that God swore, although every simple word of his is to be held as an oath. But because of men's slowness, to assure them or to stir them up, he deigns to swear, so as to intimate that what he says is unchangeably true. [[4:2|that lo, the days shall come upon you|Quia ecce dies venient super vos]], that is, the time of your captivity and affliction by the Assyrians is now at hand; [[4:2|when they shall lift you up on pikes|et levabunt vos in contis]], that is, the Assyrians will carry you off into captivity, as the flesh of fat kine is carried on poles, or heavy loads on carrying-poles [*tenellis*, apparently the medieval *tinelli*, poles for carrying a tub between two men], [[4:2|and what shall remain of you|et reliquias vestras]], that is, those left over, who flee to cities, camps or hiding places, they shall lift up [[4:2|in boiling pots|in ollis ferventibus]], that is, in the said places, in which they will have hidden as if in pots, they will burn them up by setting such places on fire: and once fired, these will be like heated or boiling pots.

paras.t: Et per aperturas exibitis, id est, de talibus locis fugietis; vel, extrahemini per quædam foramina, quæ facietis in muris sive maceriis; vel, Per aperturas, seu vias jam factas; altera contra alteram, id est, una vacca pinguis ex una parte, et alia ex parte opposita; vel, una contra aliam, id est mutuo ac vicissim. Ut enim Hieronymus dicit, idiomatis Hebræorum est, ut quod nos dicimus Mutuo, vel Vicissim, ipsi dicant Altera contra alteram. Et projiciemini, id est, captivi ducemini, in Armon, id est in Armeniam, secundum Hieronymum. Unde Symmachus transtulit, In Armeniam. Secundum Glossam, Armon est regio ultra montes Medorum atque Persarum, vel ultra terram Assyriorum, ut alii dicunt. Patet ergo, quod usque ad illud territorium translati fuerunt nonnulli de populo decem tribuum.
paras.en: [[4:3|And you shall go out at the breaches|Et per aperturas exibitis]], that is, you shall flee from such places; or, you shall be dragged out through certain holes which you will make in the walls or fences; or, [[4:3|at the breaches|Per aperturas]], that is, by ways already made; [[4:3|one over against the other|altera contra alteram]], that is, one fat cow on one side and another on the opposite side; or, one against another, that is, mutually and in turn. For, as Jerome says, it is an idiom of the Hebrews that what we call "mutually" or "in turn" they call "one over against the other". [[4:3|and you shall be cast forth|Et projiciemini]], that is, you shall be led captive, [[4:3|into Armon|in Armon]], that is, into Armenia, according to Jerome. Hence Symmachus translated: Into Armenia. According to the Gloss, Armon is a region beyond the mountains of the Medes and Persians, or, as others say, beyond the land of the Assyrians. It is plain, then, that some of the people of the ten tribes were carried away even to that territory.

paras.t: Consequenter ironice vel prænuntiative, non exhortative, ait Propheta ad decem tribus : Venite ad Bethel civitatem, in qua fuit unus de aureis vitulis, et impie agite, id est, in Deum peccate, vitulum adorando. Venite quoque ad Galgalam : in qua, quasi in celebri loco, idololatria exercebatur. Unde in Osee prædictum est: Omnis nequitia eorum in Galgalis. Et multiplicate prævaricationem, id est idololatriam vitiaque annexa. Et offerte mane victimas vestras, id est, sine dilatione sacrilegas hostias idolis immolate, quousque capiamini, tribus diebus decimas vestras. Symmachus transtulit, Tertia die. Unde sensus est, secundum Glossam : Quod prima die obtulistis, reservate in tertium diem, ut sit immundum. Ut enim Hieronymus ait, erant quædam sacrificia, de quibus nil licuit reservari in alterum diem. Et si quid reservabatur, immundum erat tam reservatum quam ipsa oblatio. Fuerunt et alia sacrificia, de quibus si usque in tertium diem aliquid reservabatur, fuit immundum : quod est immundas hostias immolare. Alii autem exponunt, dicentes quod sicut in lege præceptum fuit, ut Judæi ter in anno comparerent coram Domino in loco electo, videlicet in templo Jerusalem; sic Jeroboam primus rex decem tribuum, statuit aliqua divino cultui similia in veneratione idolorum suorum, quorum hoc exstitit unum, quod tribus diebus in anno offerebant solennes hostias idolis.
paras.en: Next the Prophet says to the ten tribes, ironically or by way of foretelling, not by way of exhortation: [[4:4|Come ye to Bethel|Venite ad Bethel]], the city in which one of the golden calves stood[[3 Kings 12:29||]], [[4:4|and do wickedly|et impie agite]], that is, sin against God by adoring the calf. Come also [[4:4|to Galgal|ad Galgalam]], in which, as in a renowned place, idolatry was practised. Hence it was foretold in Osee: [[Osee 9:15|All their wickedness is in Galgal|Omnis nequitia eorum in Galgalis]]. [[4:4|and multiply transgressions|Et multiplicate prævaricationem]], that is, idolatry and the vices joined to it. [[4:4|and bring in the morning your victims|Et offerte mane victimas vestras]], that is, sacrifice your sacrilegious victims to the idols without delay, until you are taken captive, [[4:4|your tithes in three days|tribus diebus decimas vestras]]. Symmachus translated: On the third day. Hence the sense, according to the Gloss, is: What you offered on the first day, keep over to the third day, so that it may be unclean. For, as Jerome says, there were certain sacrifices of which nothing might be kept over to the next day[[Lev 7:15||]]; and if anything was kept, both what was kept and the offering itself were unclean. There were also other sacrifices of which, if anything was kept until the third day, it was unclean[[Lev 7:18||]] [the margin gives Lev. vii, 15–18]: and this is to sacrifice unclean victims. Others, however, explain it thus: as it was commanded in the Law that the Jews should appear three times a year before the Lord in the chosen place, namely in the temple at Jerusalem, so Jeroboam, the first king of the ten tribes, set up certain things like the divine worship in the veneration of his idols, and one of these was that on three days in the year they offered solemn victims to the idols.

paras.t: Et sacrificate de fermentato laudem, id est, panem mixtum fermento offerte idolis pro gratiarum actione, quemadmodum gentiles. Lex autem prohibuit talem panem Deo offerri. Et vocate voluntarias oblationes, id est, hujusmodi sacrificia nominate hostias spontaneas: sicut in lege quædam oblationes dictæ sunt spontaneæ, quas quis offerebat ultroneus, quod ad lætitiam et supererogationem pertinuit. Et annuntiate, id est, peccata vestra aliis impudenter prædicate, ut agant similia, ut non solum fecisse, sed et alios videamini docuisse, sicut de duabus tribubus apud Isaiam legitur : Peccatum suum sicut Sodoma prædicaverunt, nec absconderunt.
paras.en: [[4:5|And offer a sacrifice of praise with leaven|Et sacrificate de fermentato laudem]], that is, offer to the idols bread mixed with leaven as a thanksgiving, as the gentiles do. But the Law forbade such bread to be offered to God. [[4:5|and call free offerings|Et vocate voluntarias oblationes]], that is, call sacrifices of this kind freewill victims: as in the Law certain offerings were called freewill offerings, which one offered of his own accord, and which belonged to gladness and to supererogation [that is, to doing more than is commanded]. [[4:5|and proclaim it|Et annuntiate]], that is, shamelessly proclaim your sins to others, so that they may do the like, and you may be seen not only to have done them but also to have taught others; as we read in Isaias of the two tribes: [[Is 3:9|they have proclaimed abroad their sin as Sodom, and they have not hid it|Peccatum suum sicut Sodoma prædicaverunt, nec absconderunt]].

paras.t: Sic enim voluistis, filii Israel, id est, hæc mala facere voluistis, et ex proposito hæc egistis: ideo locutus sum vobis ista ironice, ad insinuandum quod ista mala agendo, vobis ipsis summe nocebitis. Juxta quem modum habetur in Psalmo: Dominus regnavit, irascantur populi; in Apocalypsi quoque, Qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc.
paras.en: [[4:5|for so you would do, O children of Israel|Sic enim voluistis, filii Israel]], that is, you would do these evils, and you did them of set purpose: therefore I have said these things to you ironically, to intimate that by doing these evils you will do yourselves the greatest harm. In the same manner we find in the Psalm: [[Ps 98:1|The Lord hath reigned, let the people be angry|Dominus regnavit, irascantur populi]]; and in the Apocalypse too: [[Apoc 22:11|he that is filthy, let him be filthy still|Qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc]].

paras.t: Unde, id est propter quæ peccata, et ego Deus, justus et pius judex, dedi vobis stuporem dentium, id est dentes stupidos ex magnitudine famis, in cunctis urbibus vestris, et indigentiam panum in omnibus locis vestris, id est, fame afflixi vos. Quod enim maxima fames fuit in terra Israel tempore Eliæ et Achab, itemque tempore Elisei et Joram, innotescit in libris Regum. Et non estis reversi ad me per pœnitentiam, dicit Dominus. Tanquam dicat: Ego non ex crudelitate percussi vos fame, sed ut vexatio daret intellectum, et per flagella converteremini ad me, sed noluistis. Simile est illud quoque Isaiæ: Populus non est reversus ad percutientem se, et Dominum exercituum non exquisierunt. Et Jeremias ait: Percussisti eos, et non doluerunt, renuerunt accipere disciplinam.
paras.en: [[4:6|Whereupon|Unde]], that is, on account of which sins, [[4:6|I also|et ego]], God, the just and merciful judge[[Ps 7:12||]], [[4:6|have given you dulness of teeth|dedi vobis stuporem dentium]], that is, teeth numbed by the greatness of the hunger, [[4:6|in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places|in cunctis urbibus vestris, et indigentiam panum in omnibus locis vestris]], that is, I afflicted you with famine. For that there was a very great famine in the land of Israel in the time of Elias and Achab[[3 Kings 18:2||]], and again in the time of Eliseus[[4 Kings 4:38||]] and Joram[[4 Kings 6:25||]], is made known in the books of Kings. [[4:6|yet you have not returned to me|Et non estis reversi ad me]] by penance, [[4:6|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]. As if he said: I did not strike you with famine out of cruelty, but so that [[Is 28:19|vexation alone shall make you understand|vexatio daret intellectum]], and that through the scourges you might be converted to me; but you would not. Like this, too, is that of Isaias: [[Is 9:13|the people are not returned to him who hath struck them, and have not sought after the Lord of hosts|Populus non est reversus ad percutientem se, et Dominum exercituum non exquisierunt]]. And Jeremias says: [[Jer 5:3|thou hast struck them, and they have not grieved|Percussisti eos, et non doluerunt]]; [[Jer 5:3|they have refused to receive correction|renuerunt accipere disciplinam]].

paras.t: Ego quoque prohibui a vobis imbrem, id est pluviam serotinam, causas naturales atque cœlestes ab influxu pluviæ impediendo, quum adhuc tres menses superessent, id est restarent, usque ad messem, videlicet Maius, Junius, Julius : quo tempore pluvia ista maxime necessaria est agris Terræ sanctæ et Palæstinæ. Et plui super civitatem unam, quæ minus peccavit, et super civitatem alteram non plui. Pars una in agro compluta est, id est imbre perfusa; et pars super quam non plui, aruit, ita quod herbæ non protulerunt fructum ac triticum.
paras.en: [[4:7|I also have withholden the rain from you|Ego quoque prohibui a vobis imbrem]], that is, the latter rain, by hindering the natural and heavenly causes from the inflow of rain, [[4:7|when there were yet three months|quum adhuc tres menses superessent]], that is, were left, [[4:7|to the harvest|usque ad messem]], namely May, June and July: the season in which this rain is most needed by the fields of the Holy Land and of Palestine. [[4:7|and I caused it to rain upon on city|Et plui super civitatem unam]], which had sinned less, [[4:7|and caused it not to rain upon another city|et super civitatem alteram non plui]]. [[4:7|one piece was rained upon|Pars una in agro compluta est]], that is, drenched with rain; [[4:7|and the piece whereupon I rained not, withered|et pars super quam non plui, aruit]], so that the plants brought forth no fruit or wheat.

paras.t: Et venerunt duæ et tres civitates, super quas non plui, in quibus exsiccatæ fuerunt cisternæ, ad civitatem unam complutam, ut biberent aquam civitatis complutæ, et non sunt satiatæ, quia et modice plui super civitatem illam. Ex quibus palam est, quod istud factum non est lege naturæ, varietate temporum aut siderum cursu, sed divino miraculo, ut qui plus peccavit, gravius puniretur. Et non redistis ad me per pœnitentiam, dicit Dominus.
paras.en: [[4:8|And two and three cities went|Et venerunt duæ et tres civitates]], on which I had not rained, in which the cisterns had dried up, [[4:8|to one city|ad civitatem unam]] that had been rained on, [[4:8|to drink water|ut biberent aquam]] of the city rained on, [[4:8|and were not filled|et non sunt satiatæ]], because I rained but sparingly on that city too. From which it is plain that this was not done by the law of nature, by the changing of the seasons or the course of the stars, but by a divine miracle, so that whoever sinned more should be punished more heavily. [[4:8|yet you returned not to me|Et non redistis ad me]] by penance, [[4:8|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]].

paras.t: Tertia demum plaga annectitur. Percussi vos in vento urente, id est, in vento immoderanter calido vos afflixi, et terræ nascentia devastavi, et in aurigine, id est ærugine : quæ a Joele dicta est rubigo, scilicet vitium segetum, quando vento percussæ, non faciunt grana multa. Quandoque etiam aliter sumitur, ut dictum est plenius super Joelem. In hac ergo percussi multitudinem hortorum vestrorum et vinearum vestrarum, quas cupide multiplicastis, id est, poma et uvas destruxi. Oliveta vestra et ficeta vestra, id est fructus arborum harum, comedit eruca, id est talis vermis seu bestiola quæ non avolat, sed jacens in fructibus, totum consumit. Et non redistis ad me, dicit Dominus, quia omnia ista flagella ad vestram ordinavi emendam.
paras.en: Then the third plague is added. [[4:9|I struck you with a burning wind|Percussi vos in vento urente]], that is, I afflicted you with an immoderately hot wind and laid waste what the earth brings forth, [[4:9|and with mildew|et in aurigine]], that is, with *ærugo* [blight; Denis glosses the rare word with the common one], which Joel calls *rubigo* [mildew, or rust]: namely a disease of the crops, when, struck by the wind, they do not yield many grains. Sometimes it is also taken otherwise, as was said more fully on Joel. With this, then, I struck [[4:9|your many gardens, and your vineyards|multitudinem hortorum vestrorum et vinearum vestrarum]], which you greedily multiplied: that is, I destroyed the fruit and the grapes. [[4:9|your olive groves, and fig groves|Oliveta vestra et ficeta vestra]], that is, the fruit of these trees, [[4:9|the palmerworm hath eaten up|comedit eruca]], that is, a worm or little creature of the kind that does not fly away, but lies in the fruit and consumes it all. [[4:9|yet you returned not to me, saith the Lord|Et non redistis ad me, dicit Dominus]], for I ordained all these scourges for your amendment.

paras.t: Præterea quarta subjungitur plaga. Misi in vos mortem in via Ægypti : id est, legatos quos ad Ægyptios destinastis ad contrahendum auxilium contra Assyrios, tradidi in manus Assyriorum, qui eos in via hac occiderunt, sicut subjungitur. Percussi in gladio Assyriorum, juvenes vestros ad Ægyptum transmissos, usque ad captivitatem equorum vestrorum inclusive : quia et equos juvenum occisorum ceperunt Assyrii; et ascendere feci putredinem castrorum vestrorum, id est fœtorem cadaverum horum juvenum, quæ insepulta reliquerunt Assyrii, in nares vestras, quando ad vos delata fuerunt, vel accessistis ad ea. Et non redistis ad me, dicit Dominus.
paras.en: Moreover a fourth plague is added. [[4:10|I sent death upon you in the way of Egypt|Misi in vos mortem in via Ægypti]]: that is, the envoys whom you sent to the Egyptians to gather help against the Assyrians I delivered into the hands of the Assyrians, who killed them on that road, as is added next. [[4:10|I slew|Percussi]] [[4:10|with the sword|in gladio]] of the Assyrians [[4:10|your young men|juvenes vestros]] who were sent to Egypt, [[4:10|even to the captivity of your horses|usque ad captivitatem equorum vestrorum]] inclusively: for the Assyrians also took the horses of the young men they killed; [[4:10|and I made the stench of your camp to come up|et ascendere feci putredinem castrorum vestrorum]], that is, the stench of the corpses of these young men, which the Assyrians left unburied, [[4:10|into your nostrils|in nares vestras]], when they were brought to you, or when you came near them. [[4:10|yet you returned not to me, saith the Lord|Et non redistis ad me, dicit Dominus]].

paras.t: Postremo subjungitur quintum flagellum. Subverti vos sicut subvertit Deus Sodomam et Gomorrham : id est, tam horribiliter et districte punivi vos per Assyrios, et item per plagas memoratas, per quas et terræ nascentia demolitus sum, ita quod vestra subversio comparatur quodammodo subversioni Sodomæ et Gomorrhæ, habitatorumque earum. Nam et scelera vestra illorum criminibus erant similia. Loquitur autem Dominus de se ipso quasi de alio, dum ait : Subverti vos sicut subvertit Deus. Vel idcirco sic loquitur, ut insinuetur pluralitas Personarum in Deo, dum Pater de Deo Filio loquitur, vel econtra. Juxta quem modum loquendi scriptum est in Genesi : Dominus pluit super Sodomam et Gomorrham sulfur et ignem a Domino. Et facti estis quasi torris raptus de incendio : id est, similes facti estis ligno pro majori parte combusto, ab igne extracto ne totaliter combureretur, quoniam pauci vestrum manus hostium evaserunt. Vel hoc ideo dicitur, quia Assyrii ædificia multa decem tribuum incenderunt, de quorum incendio aliqui evaserunt. Videtur quoque Propheta in hac plaga loqui de futuro per modum præteriti. Licet enim circa tempora ejus cœperint Assyrii decem tribus opprimere, finalis tamen subversio earundem facta est tempore Osee ultimi regis Israel, quando defunctus est Amos ex dolore vulneris quod sibi inflixit filius Amasiæ sacerdotis idololatriæ, tempore Jeroboam regis filii Joas. Et non redistis ad me, dicit Dominus. De talibus tam incorrigibilibus Dominus ait per Isaiam: In quo percutiam vos ultra, addentes prævaricationem? Et item per Jeremiam : Induraverunt facies suas supra petram, et noluerunt reverti. Quem enim Deus despicit, nullus corrigit. Et nisi Deus intus operetur, tangat, afficiat, non sufficiunt extrinseca hortamenta. Isti autem ob suam perversitatem non meruerunt tangi medullitus, quia et obicem posuerunt.
paras.en: Lastly the fifth scourge is added. [[4:11|I destroyed some of you, as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrha|Subverti vos sicut subvertit Deus Sodomam et Gomorrham]] [the Latin, *Subverti vos*, is "I overthrew you"]: that is, I punished you so dreadfully and so severely through the Assyrians, and also through the plagues recorded, by which I also destroyed what the earth brings forth, that your overthrow is in some way compared with the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrha and of their inhabitants. For your crimes too were like theirs. Now the Lord speaks of himself as of another when he says: [[4:11|I destroyed some of you, as God destroyed|Subverti vos sicut subvertit Deus]]. Or he speaks so in order to intimate the plurality of Persons in God, the Father speaking of God the Son, or the other way about. In this manner of speech it is written in Genesis: [[Gen 19:24|the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire from the Lord|Dominus pluit super Sodomam et Gomorrham sulfur et ignem a Domino]]. [[4:11|and you were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning|Et facti estis quasi torris raptus de incendio]]: that is, you became like wood mostly burnt, pulled out of the fire lest it burn up altogether, since few of you escaped the hands of the enemy. Or this is said because the Assyrians burnt many buildings of the ten tribes, and some escaped from the burning of them. The Prophet also seems in this plague to speak of the future in the manner of the past. For although about his time the Assyrians began to oppress the ten tribes, yet their final overthrow took place in the time of Osee, the last king of Israel[[4 Kings 17:6||]], when Amos was already dead: he died of the pain of the wound that the son of Amasias, the priest of idolatry, inflicted on him, in the time of King Jeroboam, son of Joas. [[4:11|yet you returned not to me, saith the Lord|Et non redistis ad me, dicit Dominus]]. Of men so incorrigible the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 1:5|For what shall I strike you any more, you that increase transgression?|In quo percutiam vos ultra, addentes prævaricationem?]] And again through Jeremias: [[Jer 5:3|they have made their faces harder than the rock, and they have refused to return|Induraverunt facies suas supra petram, et noluerunt reverti]]. For whom God despises, no one corrects[[Eccles 7:14||]]. And unless God works within, touches and moves, outward exhortations are not enough. But these men, for their perversity, did not deserve to be touched to the marrow, because they also put an obstacle in the way [*obex*: the hindrance a man sets up against grace].

paras.t: Quapropter hæc faciam tibi, Israel, id est, inducam super te plagas descriptas, similes aut majores. Postquam autem hæc fecero tibi, id est, prædictas plagas induxero, præparare in occursum Dei tui, Israel. Hoc tripliciter explanatur. Primo : Præparare, id est, præpara te, in occursum Dei tui, id est ad susceptionem gratiosi adventus ejus in te : quia post captivitatem Israel ab Assyriis, quidam eorum ad Deum conversi sunt, et in Jerusalem venerunt sub Ezechia, ut dictum est. Huic sensui consonat translatio Septuaginta interpretum, quæ talis est : Præpara te, ut invoces Deum tuum, Israel. Secundo : Præparare in occursum Dei tui, id est, Unigenitum Dei verum Deum, per incarnationis mysterium in hunc mundum descendentem, devote suscipe et adora. Hoc multi ex decem tribubus impleverunt. Tertio exponitur de conversione Israel in fine sæculi, quia nec interim finitur eorum captivitas. Unde Theodotion transtulit : Novissime præparare, etc.
paras.en: [[4:12|Therefore I will do these things to thee, O Israel|Quapropter hæc faciam tibi, Israel]], that is, I will bring upon thee the plagues described, or others like them or greater. [[4:12|and after I shall have done these things to thee|Postquam autem hæc fecero tibi]], that is, when I have brought on the aforesaid plagues, [[4:12|be prepared to meet thy God, O Israel|præparare in occursum Dei tui, Israel]]. This is explained in three ways. First: [[4:12|be prepared|Præparare]], that is, prepare thyself, [[4:12|to meet thy God|in occursum Dei tui]], that is, to receive his gracious coming into thee: for after the captivity of Israel by the Assyrians, some of them were converted to God and came to Jerusalem under Ezechias[[2 Par 30:11||]], as has been said. With this sense agrees the translation of the Seventy interpreters, which runs: Prepare thyself to call upon thy God, Israel. Second: [[4:12|be prepared to meet thy God|Præparare in occursum Dei tui]], that is, devoutly receive and adore the Only-begotten of God, true God, coming down into this world through the mystery of the Incarnation. Many of the ten tribes fulfilled this. Third, it is explained of the conversion of Israel at the end of the world, since their captivity does not end in the meantime. Hence Theodotion translated: At the last, be prepared, etc.

paras.t: Porro ad hanc præparationem inducit consideratio omnipotentiæ Dei. Propter quod subditur : Quia ecce formans montes : juxta illud in Psalmo, Præparans montes in virtute tua, accinctus potentia; et creans ventum : secundum illud, Qui producit ventos de thesauris suis. Sumitur autem creatio hoc loco extense. Et annuntians homini eloquium suum, id est, sermones occultos atque propheticos electis revelans, prout jam dictum est : Non faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas. Unde et David : Incerta, inquit, et occulta sapientiæ tuæ manifestasti mihi. Eloquium quoque Domini inflammavit Joseph. Hinc per Jeremiam ait : Clama ad me, et annuntiabo tibi grandia et firma, quæ nescis.
paras.en: Now what leads to this preparation is the consideration of God's omnipotence. That is why it is added: [[4:13|For behold he that formeth the mountains|Quia ecce formans montes]]: according to that in the Psalm, [[Ps 64:7|Thou who preparest the mountains by thy strength, being girded with power|Præparans montes in virtute tua, accinctus potentia]]; [[4:13|and createth the wind|et creans ventum]]: according to that, [[Ps 134:7|He bringeth forth winds out of his stores|Qui producit ventos de thesauris suis]]. Here *creating* is taken in a wide sense. [[4:13|and declareth his word to man|Et annuntians homini eloquium suum]], that is, revealing hidden and prophetic words to the elect, as has been said already: [[Amos 3:7|the Lord God doth nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets|Non faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas]]. Hence David too: [[Ps 50:8|the uncertain|Incerta]], he says, [[Ps 50:8|and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me|et occulta sapientiæ tuæ manifestasti mihi]] [the margin gives Ps. i, 8, a misprint for Ps. l, 8]. [[Ps 104:19|The word of the Lord inflamed|Eloquium quoque Domini inflammavit]] Joseph too. Hence he says through Jeremias: [[Jer 33:3|Cry to me|Clama ad me]], [[Jer 33:3|and I will shew thee great things, and sure things which thou knowest not|et annuntiabo tibi grandia et firma, quæ nescis]].

paras.t: Faciens matutinam nebulam, quæ mane descendit, et operit terram. Omnes enim impressiones meteorologicæ sunt a Deo, tanquam a causa prima ac principali. Et gradiens super excelsa terræ. Illic Dominus graditur, ubi operatur. Ipse autem est extra omnia, et intra omnia, continens universa, et operans omnia in omnibus. Ideo ambulat per operationem super excelsa terræ, id est in montibus, quantum ad litteram. Unde et alibi legitur : Circa cardines cœli perambulat; et, Qui ambulat super pennas ventorum ; et, Graditur super fluctus maris. Dominus Deus exercituum nomen ejus. Ubi nos habemus, Exercituum, in Hebræo dicitur, Sabaoth, pro quo Septuaginta transtulerunt, Omnipotens. Unde et hoc loco dixerunt : Dominus Deus, Omnipotens nomen ejus. Utrumque enim significat Sabaoth. Dicitur autem Deus Dominus exercituum, id est cælestium agminum, imo et omnium concionum, juxta illud Isaiæ : Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; et iterum : Dominus exercituum nomen ejus. Hinc in veteri Testamento, præsertim in Zacharia, Deus Dominus exercituum appellatur.
paras.en: [[4:13|he that maketh the morning mist|Faciens matutinam nebulam]], which comes down in the morning and covers the earth. For all meteorological impressions [that is, the changes in the air: mist, dew, wind, rain] are from God as from their first and principal cause. [[4:13|and walketh upon the high places of the earth|Et gradiens super excelsa terræ]]. The Lord walks there where he works. Yet he is outside all things and within all things, containing all things, the one [[1 Cor 12:6|who worketh all in all|operans omnia in omnibus]]. So by his working he walks upon the high places of the earth, that is, on the mountains, as to the letter. Hence we read elsewhere too: [[Job 22:14|he walketh about the poles of heaven|Circa cardines cœli perambulat]]; and, [[Ps 103:3|who walkest upon the wings of the winds|Qui ambulat super pennas ventorum]]; and, [[Job 9:8|walketh upon the waves of the sea|Graditur super fluctus maris]]. [[4:13|the Lord the God of hosts is his name|Dominus Deus exercituum nomen ejus]]. Where we have *of hosts*, the Hebrew says *Sabaoth*, for which the Seventy translated *Almighty*. Hence here too they said: The Lord God, Almighty is his name. For *Sabaoth* means both. Now God is called the Lord of hosts, that is, of the heavenly armies, indeed of all assemblies, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum]]; and again: [[Is 48:2|the Lord of hosts is his name|Dominus exercituum nomen ejus]][[Is 54:5||]]. Hence in the Old Testament, and above all in Zacharias, God is called the Lord of hosts[[Zach 1:3||]].

4.title: Expositio ejusdem capituli quarti tropologica.
4.title_en: Tropological exposition of the same fourth chapter.
4.note: A few words are lost in the transcription at the start of the article (v. 1, after "in the mountains"). Please check against the scan.

paras.t: Denique vaccæ pingues in montibus […] Samariæ consistentes, quæ calumniantur egenos, confringunt pauperes, et vini pocula quærunt a superioribus suis, rite intelliguntur crudeles avarique principes populi christiani; et item carnales pastores seu prælati Ecclesiæ, qui pascunt se ipsos, lac ovium manducantes, lanamque induentes, gregem autem Domini non alentes, sed cum crudelitate atque potentia præsidentes: de quibus in Ezechiele diffuse loquitur Dominus. Isti nempe quum sint ad divina pigri, corporalem quietem vitiose amantes, vitamque bestialem ducentes in voluptatibus gulæ et luxuriæ, merito vaccæ pingues dicuntur, quia etiam quasi vacca lasciviens declinant a lege divina. De quorum singulis dici potest illud in Job: Cucurrit impius adversus Deum erecto collo, et pingui cervice armatus est.
paras.en: Lastly, the [[4:1|fat kine that are in the mountains|vaccæ pingues in montibus]] […] [[4:1|of Samaria|Samariæ]], who [[4:1|oppress the needy|calumniantur egenos]], [[4:1|crush the poor|confringunt pauperes]], and seek cups of wine from their superiors, are rightly understood as the cruel and covetous princes of the Christian people; and likewise the carnal pastors or prelates of the Church, who feed themselves, eating the milk of the sheep and clothing themselves with the wool, yet do not feed the Lord's flock, but preside over it with cruelty and might: of whom the Lord speaks at length in Ezechiel[[Ezech 34:2||]][[Ezech 34:3||]]. For these, since they are sluggish towards divine things, viciously loving bodily ease and leading a beastly life in the pleasures of gluttony and lust, are deservedly called fat kine, because they too turn aside from the divine law [[Osee 4:16|like a wanton heifer|quasi vacca lasciviens]]. Of each of them may be said that word in Job: [[Job 15:26|He hath run|Cucurrit]], the wicked man, [[Job 15:26|against|adversus]] God [[Job 15:26|with his neck raised up, and is armed with a fat neck|erecto collo, et pingui cervice armatus est]].

paras.t: Juravit Dominus: quia ecce dies venient super vos, et levabunt vos diaboli in contis, id est in suis instrumentis afflictivis, et reliquias vestras, id est corpora, quæ moriendo reliquistis, vel imitatores ac posteros, in ollis ferventibus, id est infernalibus foveis. Et projiciemini in die judicii in Armon: per quod hoc loco infernus inferior designatur. Ista fiunt reprobis in die mortis, in die judicii, et in die infernalis supplicii, quando de olla in ollam transibunt per aperturas, quia de calore nimio ad aquas nivium pergent.
paras.en: [[4:2|The Lord God hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]] [[4:2|that lo, the days shall come upon you|quia ecce dies venient super vos]], [[4:2|when they shall lift you up|et levabunt vos]], namely the devils, [[4:2|on pikes|in contis]], that is, on their instruments of torment, [[4:2|and what shall remain of you|et reliquias vestras]], that is, your bodies, which you left behind in dying, or your imitators and posterity, [[4:2|in boiling pots|in ollis ferventibus]], that is, in the pits of hell. [[4:3|you shall be cast forth|Et projiciemini]] on the day of judgment [[4:3|into Armon|in Armon]]: by which the lower hell is here signified. These things befall the reprobate on the day of death, on the day of judgment, and on the day of hell's punishment, when they shall pass from pot to pot [[4:3|at the breaches|per aperturas]], because they shall go from excessive heat to the snow waters[[Job 24:19||]] [the margin gives Ibid. xxiv, 19, that is, Job 24:19, which runs the other way: "from the snow waters to excessive heat"].

paras.t: Venite ad Bethel, id est domum seu ecclesiam Dei, et impie agite; ad Galgalam, id est Scripturarum revelationem (Galgala enim revelatio interpretatur), et multiplicate prævaricationem. Hoc ironice dicitur contra fideles qui ecclesiam visitant et sermones audiunt non ex devotione, sed arida consuetudine, vel humano pudore, aut carnali affectione, ut videant desiderabile oculorum suorum. Ideo in ecclesia et prædicatione impie agunt, et transgressiones multiplicant, effutitiones habendo, cogitationes quoque carnales, et evagationes intimoratas, et coram Sacramento irreverenter adstando.
paras.en: [[4:4|Come ye to Bethel|Venite ad Bethel]], that is, to the house or church of God, [[4:4|and do wickedly|et impie agite]]; [[4:4|to Galgal|ad Galgalam]], that is, to the revelation of the Scriptures (for Galgala is interpreted "revelation"), [[4:4|and multiply transgressions|et multiplicate prævaricationem]]. This is said ironically against the faithful who visit the church and hear sermons not out of devotion, but from dry habit, or human shame, or carnal affection, that they may see the desire of their eyes. Therefore they act wickedly in church and at preaching, and multiply transgressions, by idle babbling, by carnal thoughts too, and by wanderings of mind without fear, and by standing irreverently before the Sacrament.

paras.t: Et sacrificate de fermentato laudem, id est, per opera vitiis corrupta Deum honorate. Hoc agunt, qui faciunt opus Dei negligenter, quorum intentio sinistra, opera ex genere bona inficit; quorum divisum est cor, et conversatio prorsus immunda. Ideo monet Apostolus: Expurgate vetus fermentum, ut sitis nova conspersio.
paras.en: [[4:5|And offer a sacrifice of praise with leaven|Et sacrificate de fermentato laudem]], that is, honour God with works corrupted by vices. This is done by those who do the work of God negligently[[Jer 48:10||]] [the margin gives Jer. xlviii, 10, where the Vulgate reads *fraudulenter*, "deceitfully"], whose crooked intention infects works good in their kind; whose [[Osee 10:2|heart is divided|divisum est cor]], and whose manner of life is altogether unclean. Therefore the Apostle warns: [[1 Cor 5:7|Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new paste|Expurgate vetus fermentum, ut sitis nova conspersio]].

paras.t: Et vocate voluntarias oblationes, id est, ea quæ Deo offertis, multum reputate; et æstimate vos magnum aliquid agere, quasi condigne honoretis Deum, nec obligemini ad bona hujusmodi. Totum istud ironice dicitur. Sunt enim nonnulli, qui munera atque obsequia quæ offerunt Deo, magnifice appretiantur, et magnæ perfectionis esse se arbitrantur, quasi qui divinis beneficiis vicem idoneam præstent, non pensantes divinæ majestatis infinitam dignitatem, divinorum beneficiorum incomparabilem magnitudinem, propriæ conditionis fragilitatem, et sui obsequii imperfectionem. Contra quos ait Salvator: Quum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite: Servi inutiles sumus; quod debuimus facere, fecimus. Hinc primo Paralipomenon libro loquitur David: Tua, Domine, sunt omnia; et quæ de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi.
paras.en: [[4:5|and call free offerings|Et vocate voluntarias oblationes]], that is, set great store by what you offer to God; and reckon that you are doing something great, as though you honoured God worthily, and were not bound to good works of this kind. All this is said ironically. For there are some who value highly the gifts and services they offer to God, and think themselves of great perfection, as though they made a fitting return for God's benefits, not weighing the infinite dignity of the divine majesty, the incomparable greatness of God's benefits, the frailty of their own condition, and the imperfection of their service. Against these the Saviour says: [[Luke 17:10|when you shall have done all these things that are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which we ought to do|Quum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite: Servi inutiles sumus; quod debuimus facere, fecimus]]. Hence David says in the first book of Paralipomenon: [[1 Par 29:14|all things are thine: and we have given thee what we received of thy hand|Tua, Domine, sunt omnia; et quæ de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi]] [Denis adds "O Lord"].

paras.t: Et annuntiate aliis mala quæ facitis, ut vos imitentur et laudent in vitiis: quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ. Hoc agunt prorsus corrupti in rationis judicio et affectu, qui gloriantur quum male fecerint: de quibus scriptum est in Jeremia, Confusione non sunt confusi, et erubescere noluerunt. Sunt quoque aliqui religiosi, qui sæpe se jactant de sua audacia, rebellione atque victoria contra prælatos: quorum cæcitas et insania crassa est et magna valde.
paras.en: [[4:5|and proclaim it|Et annuntiate]] to others the evil things you do, that they may imitate you and praise you in your vices: [[Ps 9:24|For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul|quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ]] [the margin gives Ps. x, 3 according to the Hebrew, which is Ps 9:24 in the Vulgate]. This is done by those wholly corrupted in the judgment of reason and in affection, [[Prov 2:14|Who are glad when they have done evil|qui gloriantur quum male fecerint]] [Denis has *gloriantur*, "glory"]: of whom it is written in Jeremias, [[Jer 6:15|they were not confounded with confusion, and they knew not how to blush|Confusione non sunt confusi, et erubescere noluerunt]][[Jer 8:12||]] [Denis has *noluerunt*, "would not"]. There are also some religious who often boast of their boldness, rebellion and victory against their prelates: whose blindness and folly are gross and very great.

paras.t: Unde et ego dedi vobis stuporem dentium spiritualium, quibus cibus animæ masticatur atque in memoriæ ventrem projicitur: id est, robur idoneæ considerationis ac frequentis revolutionis Scripturarum sanctarum seu verborum cœlestium, tuli a vobis, in cunctis urbibus, id est congregationibus vestris. Tales nempe non gustant dulcedinem verbi Dei, nec deliciis Scripturarum pinguescunt. Hoc modo stupescunt dentes eorum qui comedunt uvam acerbam: de qua legitur, Uva eorum uva fellis, et botri amarissimi. Et indigentiam panum, id est panis sacramentalis, panis lacrimarum, panis vitæ et intellectus, panis sanctæ actionis, dedi vobis in omnibus locis vestris. His equidem panibus merentur privari, qui pascuntur in vitiis, et delectantur rebus obscœnis: quia etsi corpus Christi accipiant, non tamen spiritualiter illud manducant. Ideoque non solum non aluntur, sed gravius vacuantur et infirmantur in anima.
paras.en: [[4:6|Whereupon I also have given you dulness of teeth|Unde et ego dedi vobis stuporem dentium]], spiritual teeth, by which the food of the soul is chewed and passed into the belly of the memory: that is, I have taken from you the strength of fitting consideration and of frequent pondering of the holy Scriptures or heavenly words, [[4:6|in all your cities|in cunctis urbibus]], that is, your congregations. For such men do not taste the sweetness of the word of God, nor grow fat on the delights of the Scriptures. In this way the teeth of those who eat the sour grape are set on edge[[Jer 31:30||]] [the margin gives Ibid. xxxi, 30, that is, Jeremias]: of which we read, [[Deut 32:32|their grapes are grapes of gall, and their clusters most bitter|Uva eorum uva fellis, et botri amarissimi]]. [[4:6|and want of bread|Et indigentiam panum]], that is, of the sacramental bread, the [[Ps 79:6|bread of tears|panis lacrimarum]], the [[Ecclus 15:3|bread of life and understanding|panis vitæ et intellectus]], the bread of holy action, have I given you [[4:6|in all your places|in omnibus locis vestris]]. They indeed deserve to be deprived of these breads who feed on vices and delight in obscene things: for though they receive the body of Christ, yet they do not eat it spiritually. And so they are not only not nourished, but are more grievously emptied and weakened in soul.

paras.t: Et non estis reversi ad me, dicit Dominus. Interdum abstrahit Deus pia dispensatione etiam electis et bonis quosdam panum istorum, ne de gratia sibi data superbiant, vel per incautelam gravius ruant. Qui sentientes se pristina devotione, opulentia et alacritate privatos, mox ferventius recurrunt ad Deum; arbitrantes se illum graviter offendisse, tota intentione ad ejus pietatem confugiunt. Pristinam quoque panum spiritualium ubertatem pinguedinemque sortiti, de cetero humiliores manent et cautiores. Reprobi vero, de quibus nunc sermo, quanto spiritualibus panibus plus privantur, tanto minus ad Dominum convertuntur.
paras.en: [[4:6|yet you have not returned to me, saith the Lord|Et non estis reversi ad me, dicit Dominus]]. Sometimes God, by a loving dispensation, withdraws some of these breads even from the elect and the good, lest they grow proud of the grace given them, or through carelessness fall more grievously. They, feeling themselves deprived of their former devotion, abundance and eagerness, soon run back more fervently to God; thinking that they have grievously offended him, they flee with their whole intent to his mercy. And having regained their former plenty and richness of spiritual breads, they remain for the rest humbler and more wary. But the reprobate, of whom we now speak, the more they are deprived of spiritual breads, the less they turn to the Lord.

paras.t: Ego quoque prohibui a vobis imbrem, id est, gratiam Spiritus Sancti vobis non infudi, nec per unctionem vos docui, nec aquam sapientiæ salutaris (quæ in malevolam non ingreditur animam) vobis largitus sum. De tali imbre seu pluvia ait Salvator: Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam. Quum adhuc tres menses superessent usque ad messem, id est, quando adhuc tempus erat contritionis, confessionis et satisfactionis, quibus ad maturam æternæ beatitudinis remunerationem pertingitur. Itaque tres menses, sunt prædictæ tres partes pœnitentiæ. Et plui, id est, prædictum imbrem effudi, super civitatem unam, id est congregationem electorum atque bonorum non ponentium obicem gratiæ Dei; et super civitatem alteram reproborum et impœnitentium non plui. Pars una, id est una anima seu particularis Ecclesia, compluta est, id est cœlesti rore perfusa, et verbo doctrinæ efficaciter irrigata; et pars super quam non plui, id est anima dura seu malignantium ecclesia, aruit, tanquam arbor sterilis stirpsque inutilis. Erit enim, teste Jeremia, sicut myricæ in deserto. Hinc Christus ait in Joanne: Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras tanquam palmes, et arescet. Et pœnitens loquitur: Percussus sum ut fœnum, et aruit cor meum.
paras.en: [[4:7|I also have withholden the rain from you|Ego quoque prohibui a vobis imbrem]], that is, I have not poured into you the grace of the Holy Ghost, nor taught you by the anointing, nor bestowed on you the water of saving wisdom (which [[Wis 1:4|will not enter into a malicious soul|in malevolam non ingreditur animam]]). Of such a shower or rain the Saviour says: [[John 4:13|he that shall drink of the water that I will give him|Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei]], it [[John 4:14|shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting|fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam]]. [[4:7|when there were yet three months to the harvest|Quum adhuc tres menses superessent usque ad messem]], that is, while there was still time for contrition, confession and satisfaction, by which one attains to the ripe reward of eternal beatitude. So the three months are the three parts of penance just named. [[4:7|and I caused it to rain|Et plui]], that is, I poured out the rain spoken of, [[4:7|upon on city|super civitatem unam]], that is, upon the congregation of the elect and the good, who put no obstacle to the grace of God; [[4:7|and caused it not to rain upon another city|et super civitatem alteram]], that of the reprobate and impenitent. [[4:7|one piece|Pars una]], that is, one soul or particular Church, [[4:7|was rained upon|compluta est]], that is, was steeped in heavenly dew and effectually watered by the word of doctrine; [[4:7|and the piece whereupon I rained not|et pars super quam non plui]], that is, the hard soul or the church of the malignant, [[4:7|withered|aruit]] like a barren tree and a useless stock.
