For, as Jeremias testifies, [[Jer 17:6|he shall be|Erit enim]] [[Jer 17:6|like tamaric in the desert|sicut myricæ in deserto]]. Hence Christ says in John: [[John 15:6|If any one abide not in me, he shall be cast forth as a branch and shall wither|Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras tanquam palmes, et arescet]]. And the penitent says: [[Ps 101:5|I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered|Percussus sum ut fœnum, et aruit cor meum]].

paras.t: Et venerunt duæ et tres civitates, id est illi super quos non plui, ad civitatem unam complutam, ut biberent aquam, id est, gratiæ et sapientiæ ejus participes fierent, verbumque Dei audirent, et non sunt satiatæ. Istud accipi potest de pœnitentibus, qui non satiantur, vel quia non tantam gratiam et perfectionem consequuntur ut cupiunt, vel quia nihil gratiæ gratum facientis et donorum Spiritus Sancti participant, eo quod non vere pœniteant, et timore aut necessitate magis quam amore et voluntate hæc faciunt. Interdum quoque pluit Deus super unum, et non super alium, per nubes de quibus loquitur Isaias, Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant? id est per prædicatores et viros divinos, qui verbo tonant, miraculis coruscant, pietate obumbrant, doctrina fecundant: quando videlicet aliquibus juste verbum Dei subtrahitur, quod aliis misericorditer annuntiatur, quemadmodum Dominus ait ad Ezechielem: Fili hominis, linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo, et eris mutus, nec quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est. Faciamus ergo quod Christus ait discipulis: Rogate dominum messis, ut mittat operarios in messem suam.
paras.en: [[4:8|And two and three cities went|Et venerunt duæ et tres civitates]], that is, those upon whom I rained not, [[4:8|to one city|ad civitatem unam]] that was rained upon, [[4:8|to drink water|ut biberent aquam]], that is, to become partakers of its grace and wisdom and to hear the word of God, [[4:8|and were not filled|et non sunt satiatæ]]. This can be taken of penitents who are not filled, either because they do not obtain as much grace and perfection as they desire, or because they have no share in sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God] and the gifts of the Holy Ghost, since they do not truly repent, and do these things from fear or necessity rather than from love and good will. Sometimes too God rains upon one and not upon another through the clouds of which Isaias speaks, [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant]]? that is, through preachers and men of God, who thunder with the word, flash with miracles, overshadow with piety, make fruitful with doctrine: namely when the word of God is justly withdrawn from some which is mercifully proclaimed to others, as the Lord says to Ezechiel: Son of man, [[Ezech 3:26|I will make thy tongue stick fast to the roof of thy mouth, and thou shalt be dumb, and not as a man that reproveth: because they are a provoking house|linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo, et eris mutus, nec quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est]]. Let us do, then, what Christ said to his disciples: [[Luke 10:2|Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest that he send labourers into his harvest|Rogate dominum messis, ut mittat operarios in messem suam]].

paras.t: Percussi vos permissive, o reprobi, in vento urente, id est ardore libidinis vel doctrina ventosa et corruptiva, et in aurigine, id est ira et invidia, quæ sanguinis ruborem variant in pallorem, et fructum seminis animæ, quod est verbum Dei, corrumpunt. Percussi multitudinem hortorum vestrorum et vinearum, id est cordium, in quibus flores virtutum, gramina contemplationum, et botri fructuum Spiritus Sancti merito pullularent. Horum enim corda percutiuntur, dum a Deo relinquuntur, arescunt, vitiisque subduntur. Oliveta vestra et ficeta, id est opera misericordiæ et suavitatis internæ vel habitus virtuosos, ex quibus procedunt hujusmodi actus, quemadmodum fructus prodeunt ex arboribus, comedit eruca, id est mordax ac pungitiva invidia, quæ omnia vastat, si admittatur: non enim compati aut auxiliari permittit.
paras.en: [[4:9|I struck you|Percussi vos]], by permission, O reprobate, [[4:9|with a burning wind|in vento urente]], that is, with the heat of lust or with windy and corrupting doctrine, [[4:9|and with mildew|et in aurigine]], that is, with anger and envy, which change the redness of the blood into pallor, and corrupt the fruit of the soul's seed, which is the word of God[[Luke 8:11||]]. I struck [[4:9|your many gardens, and your vineyards|multitudinem hortorum vestrorum et vinearum]], that is, your hearts, in which the flowers of the virtues, the grasses of contemplation, and the clusters of the fruits of the Holy Ghost should rightly have sprung up. For the hearts of these are struck when they are forsaken by God, wither, and are made subject to vices. [[4:9|your olive groves, and fig groves|Oliveta vestra et ficeta]], that is, the works of mercy and of inward sweetness, or the virtuous habits from which such acts proceed, as fruits come forth from trees, [[4:9|the palmerworm hath eaten up|comedit eruca]], that is, biting and stinging envy, which lays all waste if it is let in: for it does not allow one to pity or to help.

paras.t: Misi in vos mortem in via Ægypti: id est, quum ambularetis in operibus carnis et sæculi, vita gratiæ vos privavi, vel corporaliter castigavi. Percussi in gladio juvenes vestros. Gladius spiritus est verbum Dei. Qui ergo in juventute ex auditu verborum Dei corrigitur, gladio salubriter verberatur. Usque ad captivitatem equorum, id est refrenationem lascivorum motuum corporis. Hæc quoque aliter accipi possunt, sed propter causam pertranseo.
paras.en: [[4:10|I sent death upon you in the way of Egypt|Misi in vos mortem in via Ægypti]]: that is, when you walked in the works of the flesh and of the world, I deprived you of the life of grace, or chastised you in body. [[4:10|I slew your young men with the sword|Percussi in gladio juvenes vestros]]. The [[Eph 6:17|sword of the Spirit|Gladius spiritus]] is [[Eph 6:17|the word of God|verbum Dei]]. He then who in youth is corrected by hearing the words of God is wholesomely smitten with the sword. [[4:10|even to the captivity of your horses|Usque ad captivitatem equorum]], that is, to the bridling of the wanton movements of the body. These things can also be taken otherwise, but for good reason I pass over it.

paras.t: Subverti vos sicut subvertit Deus Sodomam et Gomorrham, id est, igne concupiscentiæ et sulfure fœtidissimæ voluptatis prorsus permisi vos perire, quantum ad spirituale esse gratiæ gratificantis, et facti estis quasi torris raptus de incendio, quantum ad hoc quod nondum pœnas tartarei ignis incidistis. Et non redistis ad me: in quo patet incorrigibilitas vestra. De talibus Dominus ait ad Jeremiam: Quare aversus est populus iste aversione contentiosa?
paras.en: [[4:11|I destroyed some of you, as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrha|Subverti vos sicut subvertit Deus Sodomam et Gomorrham]], that is, I let you perish utterly by the fire of concupiscence and the brimstone of most foul pleasure, as regards the spiritual being of sanctifying grace, [[4:11|and you were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning|et facti estis quasi torris raptus de incendio]], inasmuch as you have not yet fallen into the pains of the fire of hell. [[4:11|yet you returned not to me|Et non redistis ad me]]: in which your incorrigibility is plain. Of such the Lord says to Jeremias: [[Jer 8:5|Why then is this people in Jerusalem turned away with a stubborn revolting?|Quare aversus est populus iste aversione contentiosa?]]?

paras.t: Quia ecce formans montes, id est, angelos sanctos in sublimitate naturæ et gratiæ atque in beatifica fruitione constituens. Vel, montes, id est Apostolos et imitatores eorum in arce virtutum reponens, quorum conversatio est in cœlis; et sicut exaltantur cœli a terra, ita exaltatur nobilis angelica cœliformisque vita eorum, ab ignobili, confusa et injusta malorum Christianorum conversatione, de qualibus dicitur, Recedentes a te, in terra scribentur. Et creans ventum, id est eos qui velocissime cuncta terrena transcendunt.
paras.en: [[4:13|For behold he that formeth the mountains|Quia ecce formans montes]], that is, establishing the holy angels in the height of nature and of grace and in the beatific enjoyment. Or, the mountains, that is, the Apostles and their imitators, setting them in the citadel of the virtues, whose [[Phil 3:20|conversation is in heaven|conversatio est in cœlis]]; and [[Is 55:9|as the heavens are exalted above the earth|sicut exaltantur cœli a terra]], so is their noble, angelic and heavenly life exalted above the ignoble, disordered and unjust conversation of bad Christians, of whom it is said, [[Jer 17:13|they that depart from thee, shall be written in the earth|Recedentes a te, in terra scribentur]]. [[4:13|and createth the wind|Et creans ventum]], that is, those who most swiftly pass beyond all earthly things.

paras.t: Faciens matutinam nebulam, id est, symbolicarum revelationum obscuritate in primis mentem involvens, antequam ad anagogicæ contemplationis perveniat puritatem. Ita fit sæpe. Hæc ergo obscuritas, per nebulam quæ mane operit terram, significatur. Non enim possibile est aliter nobis lucere divinum radium, nisi variis sensibilium formarum velaminibus circumtectum. Et gradiens super excelsa terræ, id est, in mentibus contemplativis atque theoricis ambulans, cum quibus esse, sunt deliciæ meæ. Ecce tanta est conventio, communio atque concordia Dei cum servulis suis devotis atque humilibus. Cum exsistentibus est, cum stantibus stat, cum habitantibus habitat, cum gradientibus graditur, cum ascendentibus et descendentibus ascendit atque descendit. Hinc ait ad Jacob in Genesi: Ego descendam tecum in Ægyptum. Et Jacob loquens de ipso: Deus, inquit, qui socius fuit itineris mei. Dat enim suis virtutem ad omnia ista, eosque in cunctis gratiose deducit. Nec hoc solum, sed ipsi quoque sunt, manent, stant, ambulant, ascendunt atque descendunt in ipso, id est secundum voluntatem, et per gratiam ejus.
paras.en: [[4:13|he that maketh the morning mist|Faciens matutinam nebulam]], that is, first wrapping the mind in the obscurity of symbolic revelations before it comes to the purity of anagogical contemplation [that is, contemplation that rises to heavenly things]. So it often happens. This obscurity, then, is signified by the mist that covers the earth in the morning. For it is not possible for the divine ray to shine on us otherwise than veiled about with the various coverings of sensible forms. [[4:13|and walketh upon the high places of the earth|Et gradiens super excelsa terræ]], that is, walking in contemplative and speculative minds, with whom [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be|esse, sunt deliciæ meæ]]. See how great is the agreement, fellowship and concord of God with his devout and humble little servants. With those who exist he is, with those who stand he stands, with those who dwell he dwells, with those who walk he walks, with those who go up and go down he goes up and goes down. Hence he says to Jacob in Genesis: [[Gen 46:4|I will go down with thee|Ego descendam tecum]] into Egypt. And Jacob, speaking of him: God, he says, who [[Gen 35:3|accompained me in my journey|socius fuit itineris mei]]. For he gives his own the strength for all these things, and graciously leads them in all. And not only this, but they too are, remain, stand, walk, go up and go down in him, that is, according to his will, and through his grace.
